check_text:
protocol.py: 1 biology problem (1 error).

1. ERROR SOURCE-TOO-SHALLOW: The pipette draws air from well A1 in slot 4: the liquid is
below the tip
   line 39:  p300.aspirate(diluent_volumes[i], reservoir["A1"])
   At line 39 the p300_single_gen2 draws 37.18 ul from water (well A1 in slot 4) with its
   tip 1 mm above the bottom of the well. By then the well holds 1,146 ul, which in this
   NEST 1 Well Reservoir 195 mL reaches only 0.88 mm up: the tip is above the liquid and
   draws air (this line did it 4 times, after 20 times in the liquid; 170 ul of air in all).
   The simulator does not notice: it does not follow the liquid. The 4 wells filled from
   these draws got air instead of liquid.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 4.
   Also reached 4 other wells: wells B9, B10, B11 and B12 in slot 3.
   Fix: Keep the liquid above the tip. This well needs about 1,766 ul in it for the surface
   to reach 1 mm. Load that much more than the run draws; or draw from a smaller vessel (a
   tube lifts the liquid); or aspirate lower with `well.bottom(0.5)`.
   Source: Opentrons: liquid control (aspirates 1 mm above the bottom of the well by
   default)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/basic_commands/liquids.html
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Gilson guide to pipetting (immersion depth 2 to 3 mm for 1 to 100 ul)
           https://solutions.pipette.com/wp-content/uploads/Gilson-Guide-to-Pipetting.pdf
   Source: labautomation.io 7592: negative controls positive after aspirating air
           https://labautomation.io/t/aspiration-dispense-liquid-class-incompatibity/7592
   Source: Integra: 260 ul dead volume in a standard reservoir
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applications/minimizing-dead-volume-during-qpcr-set-divided-reservoir-assist-plus-pipetting-robot
   [3597ac9ebac6]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.

findings.title: The pipette draws air from well A1 in slot 4: the liquid is below the tip
findings.explanation: At line 39 the p300_single_gen2 draws 37.18 ul from water (well A1 in slot 4) with its tip 1 mm above the bottom of the well. By then the well holds 1,146 ul, which in this NEST 1 Well Reservoir 195 mL reaches only 0.88 mm up: the tip is above the liquid and draws air (this line did it 4 times, after 20 times in the liquid; 170 ul of air in all). The simulator does not notice: it does not follow the liquid. The 4 wells filled from these draws got air instead of liquid.
findings.fix: Keep the liquid above the tip. This well needs about 1,766 ul in it for the surface to reach 1 mm. Load that much more than the run draws; or draw from a smaller vessel (a tube lifts the liquid); or aspirate lower with `well.bottom(0.5)`.
